layout: row-major, north-up, same grid as elev.bin

classes.name: unknown (no colour imagery: panchromatic strip of the mosaic, or no data)
classes.factor_source: Unmapped, assumed firm (factor 1.0). No terrain class could be assigned here.

classes.name: firm ground (bedrock, consolidated regolith)
classes.factor_source: Pandolf, Givoni & Goldman 1977 / Soule & Goldman 1972 terrain coefficient eta = 1.0 (blacktop road or treadmill), i.e. the reference surface of the walking model; table reproduced in Potter et al. 2013, J Sport Hum Perf 1(3):34-42, https://jhp-ojs-tamucc.tdl.org/jhp/article/view/jshp.0009.2013/pdf . Bedrock itself was never measured; equating it with firm road is our assumption (eta = 1.1 "dirt road" is the next category).

classes.name: loose sand (dark aeolian sand, ripples, sand sheets)
classes.factor_source: eta = 2.1 "loose sand", Soule & Goldman 1972 (J Appl Physiol 32:706) as used in Pandolf et al. 1977 (J Appl Physiol 43:577); quoted in Potter et al. 2013 https://jhp-ojs-tamucc.tdl.org/jhp/article/view/jshp.0009.2013/pdf (measured ratios 1.84-2.45: Richmond, Potter & Santee 2015, https://jhp-ojs-tamucc.tdl.org/jhp/article/view/67/pdf_17). Independent check: Lejeune, Willems & Heglund 1998, J Exp Biol 201:2071, "walking on sand requires 2.1-2.7 times more energy expenditure than does walking on a hard surface at the same speed", https://europepmc.org/article/MED/9622579

classes.name: rough ground (DEM: >0.15 m relief inside the 3 m cell; scarps, ledges, blocky ground)
classes.factor_source: Voloshina, Kuo, Daley & Ferris 2013, J Exp Biol 216:3963, uneven terrain raised net metabolic rate by 28% (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4236228); upper bound: Gast, Kram & Riemer 2019, J Exp Biol 222:jeb185447, cost of transport ~115% higher on a rocky trail and preferred speed 1.07 vs 1.24 m/s (speed_factor 0.86), https://europepmc.org/article/MED/30910832

factor_usage: terrain_factor multiplies the LOCOMOTION part of the metabolic energy of entering a cell. In Pandolf et al. 1977, M = 1.5W + 2.0(W+L)(L/W)^2 + eta(W+L)(1.5V^2 + 0.35VG): eta scales only the walking term, not the standing/basal terms (equation and term definitions: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandolf_equation ; Earth-gravity coefficients; no 0.38 g data exist). Not flagged as sand does NOT mean firm: sand recall is only ~0.6. Only class 3 has a sourced speed reduction; a time penalty for sand is NOT given by these sources (Lejeune measured at equal speed).

model.name: TETHER terrain-AI v1
model.sand_classifier: Gradient-boosted trees (scikit-learn HistGradientBoosting) on per-cell features: dinov2-small_rgb_3m+12m+colour+texture+dem
model.backbone: DINOv2-small (Meta AI, self-supervised ViT-S/14, facebook/dinov2-small), frozen, run on the RGB HiRISE image twice: 1 ViT patch = 1 planning cell (3 m) and 1 patch = 4x4 cells (12 m, bilinearly upsampled); each PCA to 24 dims
model.extra_features: HiRISE colour chromaticity and relative brightness, 0.5 m texture, slope, topographic position index (9/33/75 m), 1 m roughness
model.training_labels: 497 decided visually interpreted cells: 347 from the stratified 20x20 check grid (53 unsure excluded) + 150 targeted training-only cells (200 drawn, 50 unsure excluded)
model.nasa_benchmark_cnn: ResNet-18 fine-tuned on the NASA JPL HiRISE landmark data set v3.2 (dune detector); good benchmark score but weak transfer to this AOI, see metrics

metrics.test_accuracy_note: Development spatial-block CV of the SHIPPED map (same post-processing applied to the out-of-fold probability map) on the visually labelled check cells that are clear from orbit. The check set also guided feature-set choice, so this is a development score, not a pristine test. Compare with all_firm_baseline_accuracy.
metrics.cv_protocol: 5-fold spatial block CV (5x5 macro-blocks of ~640 m; folds = whole blocks), 3x3-cell label expansion in training only

nasa_landmark_benchmark.note: ResNet-18 on the NASA JPL HiRISE landmark data set v3.2, held-out source-image-disjoint test split. NOT used in the shipped map (weak transfer: AUC ~0.56-0.69 on AOI sand vs firm).

navcam_ground_truth.method: Downward-looking Navcam frame (lowest mast elevation, ~-17 to -28 deg) at 60 end-of-drive waypoints, ground visually labelled firm / mixed / sand / not visible (deck-only frames). Compared with the map in the 15 m x 15 m box around the rover (predicted sand if >=20% of the box is class 2).

method: 1) Lock a spatially stratified check set (400 cells, 20x20 jittered grid) and label it visually from 48 m HiRISE crops (sand / firm / unsure) BEFORE any model output. 2) Extract frozen DINOv2 embeddings of the RGB image at two scales (one ViT patch = one 3 m cell, and = 12 m), plus colour, texture and DEM features. 3) Train a gradient-boosted classifier for sand vs firm; score it with 5-fold spatial block cross-validation (whole ~640 m blocks held out), then post-process (p>0.5, 2x2 opening, no isolated sand on slopes >33 deg (assumed repose limit), panchromatic strip -> unknown) and re-score the post-processed out-of-fold map. 4) Class 3 (rough) is NOT learned: it is 1 m DEM relief inside the 3 m cell > 0.15 m. 5) Check against Curiosity: class at its 257 end-of-drive positions, and Navcam ground photos at 60 of them. 6) Separately, a ResNet-18 trained on NASA JPL's labelled HiRISE data set was tested as a dune detector on this area (benchmark accuracy reported; transfer is weak, so it is not used in the final map).
sources: HiRISE LRGB mosaic of Gale (USGS Astrogeology; HiRISE NASA/JPL/University of Arizona)
USGS MSL Gale DEM mosaic 1 m v3
Doran, G., Wagstaff, K. et al. (2020) Mars orbital image (HiRISE) labeled data set version 3.2, Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.4002935 (via Mars-Bench, Hugging Face Mirali33/mb-landmark_cls, CC-BY-4.0)
Oquab, M. et al. (2023) DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision, arXiv:2304.07193 (weights facebook/dinov2-small, Apache-2.0)
He, K. et al. (2016) Deep residual learning (ResNet-18, torchvision ImageNet weights)
Curiosity waypoints (NASA/JPL MMGIS) and Navcam raw images (NASA/JPL-Caltech)
Terrain factors: Soule & Goldman 1972; Pandolf et al. 1977; Lejeune et al. 1998; Voloshina et al. 2013; Gast et al. 2019 (URLs in classes[])
caveats: Training and check labels are visual photo-interpretation of 0.5 m HiRISE crops made with an AI assistant (Claude), not by a planetary geologist; a team member can audit them in pipeline/vision/labels/. Only 38 of 347 scored check cells are sand, so sand precision/recall have wide uncertainty (roughly +/-0.1).

Colour carries most of the signal: the no-deep-learning baseline (colour + texture + DEM) scores about the same AUC as the DINOv2 model (differences are within noise with 38 sand cells). Sand recall is ~0.6: tan, dust-coloured ripple fields and sand between rock blocks are often missed, so "not flagged" does not mean firm.
The 53 check cells labelled unsure (often blue-grey knobby ground) are not scored; the Navcam site 125_2490 suggests that ground type is often sandy.

The check set guided model selection (12 feature sets compared, a 12 m pass added, batch-3 training cells sampled where tan ripples were missed), so the CV score is a development score. The Navcam comparison is the only untouched evidence, and it has only 5 sand sites.

Dark-toned bedrock and thin sand veneers over rock look alike from orbit; shadows on steep slopes can look like dark sand. Curiosity drove over sandy ground at the south end of the traverse (Navcam sites 124-125); the map flags 3 of the 5 sandy Navcam sites.

The west strip and a small south-edge patch of the mosaic are panchromatic (no colour, ~6% of the AOI). There the sand model flagged dark rough rock as sand, so those cells (plus a 2-cell seam) are class 0 unknown; only the DEM-derived rough class is kept there.
Rough class is a DEM threshold, not validated against ground truth; HiRISE DEM noise (~0.1-0.2 m) adds false rough cells.
Terrain factors are Earth-gravity energy coefficients for unsuited walkers; no validated 0.38 g suited-walking terrain data exist.
